d.t: To cross out with a series of the letter X, or with scribbles or lines.
d.e: On a close to final copy the title The Way We Die Now has Now Xed out and replaced with Today. Then Today is Xed out and Now is returned to its place.

d.t: To close a window (typically by clicking a button marked with an X symbol).
d.e: When you have selected your desired settings, X out of the window and return to the document.

d.t: The logic function exclusive OR (as opposed to inclusive OR), whose output is true only when exactly one of its inputs is true.
The connective "exclusive or". One way to state its meaning in plain English is "if either A or B, but not if both."
d.e: The XOR of (0,0) is 0; (0,1) is 1; (1,0) is 1; and (1,1) is 0.

d.t: A logic gate that implements "exclusive or".
The symbolic representation that implements "exclusive or".
d.e: XOR can be used to add bits without carrying.
The argument leads to the conclusion that an omnipotent being could rationally be able to do one xor the other and still be omnipotent.

d.t: To perform the XOR function upon.
d.e: The XORed sequence has the same period as the sequence that is not XORed.

d.t: A fictional monster that devours earthen and silicate materials and can move freely through earth.
d.e: Various monsters can tunnel through rock - either humanoid monsters with picks or rock eaters like rock moles and umber hulks; and some monsters like xorns and ghosts can pass through it without digging.

d.t: An abbreviation for hugs and kisses, usually placed at the end of a letter.
